proposals.downside_risk: Asynchronous chain states or diverging bridge liquidity could trap positions if cross-chain execution fails or bridging costs outweigh the dislocation edge.

evidence.detail: Existing signals handle cross-venue net arbitrage and forecasted positive net edge, but lack explicit relative value evaluation between the same asset bridging Solana and EVM.

proposals.expected_effect: A new independent source of eligible opportunities in high-volatility market regimes, uncorrelated with leader-copy signals.
proposals.rationale: With the cross-chain strategy framework explicitly decoupling Solana/EVM costs, an opportunity exists to model pure relative value dislocations on identical assets before structural mean reversion, without single-wallet dependency.
proposals.shadow_test: Record simultaneous simulated entries on both chains against theoretical bridging/hedging costs and measure net basis point edge post-latency. Falsified if net edge is consistently negative due to divergent gas and priority fees.

rejected_ideas.idea: Promote Liquidity Confirmed Momentum to CANARY or LIVE
rejected_ideas.reason: Promotion is forbidden due to missing runtime forensics; independent validation of live costs is currently impossible.

summary: Runtime forensics are missing, so no strategy can be claimed profitable or canary-ready. Based on architectural review of the Strategy Lab, we propose introducing a new shadow test for cross-chain relative value tracking to enhance our suite of market-native predictive hypotheses.
